summary: Malaysia grants visa-free entry to most nationalities — for visits of less than a month for ASEAN neighbors except Myanmar, up to 30 days per entry for Chinese citizens (visa-free from 1 September 2026), and for social visits by Indian citizens (exemption until 31 December 2026) — and the Immigration Department requires foreign visitors, except Singapore citizens, diplomatic and official passport holders and some residents and border-pass holders, to complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC), which Canada's travel advice says is free and can be filled in up to 3 days before arrival.

declarations.name: Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC)
declarations.submitWindow: Within 3 days before arrival, including the day you submit it
declarations.text: The Immigration Department requires visitors to complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) at imigresen-online.imi.gov.my; it exempts Singapore citizens, diplomatic and official passport holders, Malaysian permanent residents and long-term pass holders, and holders of certain Brunei, Thai and Indonesian border documents. The MDAC registration form says your trip must be within 3 days, including the date of submission. Canada's travel advice says it is free and must be presented with your passport at immigration, and warns against websites that charge fees for it.

safety.text: The UK government says bag-snatching is common in major cities, often by thieves on motorbikes, and that credit card and ATM fraud is widespread. It advises against all but essential travel to the islands and dive sites off eastern Sabah, from Sandakan to Tawau, because of the threat of kidnapping; this does not apply to the Sabah mainland.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says the MDAC is free, reports an increase in online scams around it, and advises not to use any website that charges fees for arrival cards and to apply only on the official website (imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac).

The UK says Malaysia has a zero-tolerance policy on drug offences, with penalties that include long jail sentences, possible whipping and a possible death sentence for trafficking, and that you may be asked for a urine test on arrival.
The UK says you must carry your passport when travelling between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah or Sarawak (Malaysian Borneo): you pass through immigration control and get entry and exit stamps.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Malaysia?
faq.answer: No. The US is not on the Immigration Department's list of nationalities that need a visa; the Department does not publish how long US citizens may stay. Visitors must also complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) online, which Canada's travel advice says is free and can be filled in up to 3 days before arrival.

faq.question: What is the MDAC and who needs it?
faq.answer: The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card is the online arrival form at imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac that the Immigration Department requires visitors to complete. Canada's travel advice says it is free and can be filled in up to 3 days before arrival.

faq.question: Can Chinese and Indian citizens visit Malaysia without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes. From 1 September 2026, Chinese citizens on ordinary or public affairs passports valid for at least 6 months can enter visa-free for social visits of up to 30 days per entry. Indian citizens are exempt from the visa for social visits until 31 December 2026. Both must also complete the MDAC.

faq.question: How much does a Malaysia eVisa cost?
faq.answer: For the nationalities that need one (including Pakistani and Nigerian citizens), the eVisa costs a RM105 processing charge plus a visa fee that depends on nationality and a convenience charge of 0.8% (card) or 1.7% (Alipay, WeChat Pay). The official portal malaysiavisa.imi.gov.my says processing takes 2 to 7 working days.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Malaysia?
faq.answer: No official Malaysian source we could read gives seasonal guidance. The CIA World Factbook describes two monsoons, the southwest from April to October and the northeast from October to February, and Canada's travel advice gives the rainy season as November to March, when flooding and landslides can disrupt travel.
